correctness.rationale: For every allowed sequence, classical-field segments preserve cavity photon number. Before any quantum-field segment, an occupied cavity level at most \(M\) combined with the qutrit can have total excitation at most \(M+2\). The quantum-field Hamiltonian commutes with total excitation, so afterward the cavity cannot occupy any level above \(M+2\). Induction gives support at most \(2k\) after \(k\) quantum-field segments. Because \(|N,gangle\) is in the allowed target class, \(k\ge\lceil N/2ceil\). The source construction processes two excitation blocks per quantum-field segment and handles odd parity, attaining the bound. The finite checker was replayed successfully but is not used as the proof.

value.rationale: The exact lower bound resolves a natural efficiency question left implicit by a new constructive protocol: within the stated alternating Hamiltonian architecture, the advertised factor-two reduction cannot be improved in quantum-field segment count. This is useful structurally because it identifies the precise resources that must change to beat the bound: ancilla excitation span, photon-changing interaction order, or channel alternation. The statement does not rely on a tiny numerical improvement or an arbitrary parameter slice.
